lines.t: This game sold two million copies in under five days, and its studio almost didn't survive to make it.
Wardogs is a 100 player shooter. Three teams fight to hold one control zone on a giant map.
Everything runs on in-game cash. You start with 10,000 dollars, and every gun and vehicle has a price.

sc.label: YOU START WITH
sc.sub: every gun and vehicle costs cash

lines.t: You earn more by fighting, reviving, driving and building.
Players even started running their own paid taxi services.
Buildings can be destroyed, and voice chat is heard by all three teams.
Three days after launch it peaked at over 428,000 players on Steam.
The map is a fictional country, modelled on the real country of Georgia.

sc.label: GEORGIA: THE REAL PLACE BEHIND THE MAP

lines.t: The studio, Bulkhead, needed just 400,000 sales to survive. It sold a million on day one.
A bigger publisher passed on the pitch, so they signed with Team17 instead.
There's no battle pass and no microtransactions. The developers even published ten reasons not to buy it.
And the boss says cash is the best anti-cheat.
It's in early access, only on PC, for 40 dollars.
Would you be a soldier, or a taxi driver? Follow for more!
